channel.title: Hemang Champaneria
channel.description: Essays by Hemang Champaneria on being a good human, and notes for young entrepreneurs.

item.title: Kindness is a business skill
item.description: Kindness is not softness, and it is not the same as being liked. It is a practical skill that makes it cheaper to tell the truth early.

item.title: What I’d tell myself at 22 about money
item.description: Money is not mainly about how much you can make. It is about not getting surprised, and about the gap between what comes in and what goes out.

item.title: How to treat the people who work with you
item.description: The people who work with you are not a cost to be squeezed. They are the work, and how you treat them is the culture, whether you write it down or not.

item.title: On leading by listening
item.description: The people closest to a problem usually see it first. Listening is not a pause before the work of leading. It is the work.

item.title: On keeping a small operation steady
item.description: Most small operations strain when the ordinary work is sloppy. A few simple habits do more than a complicated plan.

item.title: On community
item.description: Community is built in ordinary ways: keeping a promise, noticing who needs a hand, and giving time.

item.title: On making time for real work
item.description: It is easy to stay busy and still postpone the work that matters. Real work needs unbroken time, and a decision to protect it.
